rationale:
Split into four children: three new ones and one reused accepted theorem.

The selected proof bundles three reusable analytic facts with a short topological transport:
(1) uniform approximation of continuous compactly supported covector fields by test forms with prescribed support (step 3);
(2) the Cauchy estimate and choice-independent limit of T along such approximations (steps 4–5);
(3) the algebra of approximating sequences. It gives a linear extension Φ of T to compactly supported continuous fields on ℝ^P that agrees with T and satisfies the local bound (steps 2–3, 5–8).

What remains for the parent is the zero extension g ↦ g̃ = c⁻¹∘g from ↥U to ℝ^P (steps 1, 7, 8). Mathlib covers it: HasCompactSupport.continuous_extend_zero, extend_zero, tsupport_extend_zero_subset and exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure, all in scope after import GMT.Ch07.Submission.

Φ is the standard extension of a current with locally finite mass to C_c forms (Simon 6.2 / Federer 4.1.5), so the pieces are reusable. Splitting is also much safer. leaf_verification.check_source_delta lets a leaf append exactly one theorem and no helper declarations, so a monolithic proof would be one ~400-line declaration. The verified pieces are about 45 (uniform_approx), 90 (limit_functional) and 150 (ambient_extension) lines, plus a roughly 120-line parent assembly.

- mollify_unit_field is the accepted dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field (candidate 8abce32), reused with its identical frozen type exactly as in the parent mass_representation decomposition. Only uniform_approx depends on it.

- limit_functional (cmr_tfe_exists_limit_functional): no dependencies.
- ambient_extension (cmr_tfe_ambient_extension): depends on uniform_approx and limit_functional.
The graph is acyclic and the children sit at depth 4 (limit 6).

Mass-bound interface. This node's prerequisite eval_mass_bound (cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn) is unaccepted (status decomposing) and owned by the sibling branch. So runtime._existing_lean_name_problem forbids listing it as a child here, and a child worktree overlays only its own sibling dependencies (runtime._overlay_accepted_children). limit_functional and ambient_extension therefore take an arbitrary m : Set (Euclid P) → ℝ with exactly the shape of eval_mass_bound's conclusion.

The selected node keeps its depends_on (eval_mass_bound, mollify_unit_field); its proof overlay includes both children and depends_on. It instantiates m W := (T.massOn W).toReal. Property (ii) then comes from conjunct (d), whose proof applies the m-bound to the approximants with r + 1/(k+1) and passes to the limit. The supplied step 8 instead uses approximants with |ω_k| ≤ 1 and le_massOn on ±ω_k. Both are uses of the same mass bound, and the deviation is intended.

subproblems.title: Uniform smooth approximation of continuous unit covector fields (accepted theorem, reused)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with operator norm ‖·‖, and |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Let g : ℝ^P → Λ be continuous with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ V and |g(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Let ε > 0. Then there is an n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ that is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω), with tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), IsOpen V → Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ V → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (g x) ≤ 1) → 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - g x) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem of DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.smooth_unit_approximation-a1.mollify_unit_field-a1, reused with its identical frozen type. Its proof is reproduced here (mollification), with the coefficient isometry written out.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with the operator norm ‖·‖; |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm; e_I := (e_{I 0}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) for the standard basis e of ℝ^P.
1. (Norm facts.) Let A : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P), A α := (if StrictMono I then α(e_I) else 0)_I. A is linear and continuous, since |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖. By the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm and EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, |α| = ‖A α‖. Let C₀ := ‖A‖. Then |α| ≤ C₀‖α‖, and |·| inherits the triangle inequality and homogeneity from the Euclidean norm.
2. (Support margin.) tsupport g is compact and contained in the open set V. So there is r > 0 with cthickening r (tsupport g) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).
3. (Uniform continuity.) g is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous. Choose s₀ > 0 with ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(C₀ + 1) whenever dist(y, x) < s₀, and put s := min(s₀, r) > 0.
4. (Kernel.) Let φ be a smooth bump on ℝ^P centred at 0 with inner radius s/2 and outer radius s (ContDiffBump). Then φ is C^∞, 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, φ = 1 on closedBall(0, s/2) and support φ = ball(0, s). Its integral J := ∫ φ is positive (φ ≥ 0 and φ = 1 on a ball of positive measure) and finite. Then ψ := J⁻¹φ is C^∞, ψ ≥ 0, ∫ ψ = 1, support ψ = ball(0, s), and tsupport ψ = closedBall(0, s) is compact.
5. (Definition.) Let ω(x) := ∫ ψ(t)•g(x − t) dt, the convolution ψ ⋆ g. This is a Bochner integral in the complete space Λ, and for each x the integrand is continuous with compact support in t.
6. (Smoothness.) ψ is C^∞ with compact support and g is continuous, hence locally integrable. So ω is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
7. (Support.) support ω ⊆ support ψ + support g ⊆ thickening(s, tsupport g). Hence tsupport ω ⊆ cthickening(s, tsupport g) ⊆ cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V, and ω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution). So IsTestForm ω and tsupport ω ⊆ V.
8. (|ω| ≤ 1.) A commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm). So |ω(x)| = ‖A ω(x)‖ = ‖∫ ψ(t)·A(g(x − t)) dt‖ ≤ ∫ ψ(t)|g(x − t)| dt ≤ ∫ ψ = 1.
9. (Approximation.) Since ∫ ψ = 1, ω(x) − g(x) = ∫ ψ(t)•(g(x − t) − g(x)) dt. Here ψ(t) ≠ 0 only when ‖t‖ < s ≤ s₀, and then ‖g(x − t) − g(x)‖ < ε/(C₀ + 1). Hence ‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ ε/(C₀ + 1), and by step 1, |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ C₀ε/(C₀ + 1) ≤ ε.
10. Steps 6–9 show that ω is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere and |ω − g| ≤ ε everywhere.
proof_key_steps: The coefficient map A gives |α| = ‖Aα‖ ≤ ‖A‖·‖α‖.
Choose r > 0 with cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V; by uniform continuity choose 0 < s ≤ r with ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(‖A‖+1) whenever dist(y, x) < s.
Convolve g with a normalized smooth bump ψ of radius s: ω = ψ ⋆ g is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ cthickening(s, tsupport g) ⊆ V.
A commutes with the integral, so |ω(x)| ≤ ∫ ψ(t)|g(x − t)| dt ≤ 1.

subproblems.title: Uniform approximation of continuous compactly supported covector fields by test forms supported in an open set (parent step 3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ and let c : Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n → ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be a continuous linear equivalence with covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ for every α ∈ Λ. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let G : ℝ^P → Λ be continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ V, and let ε > 0. Then there is an n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ that is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω), with tsupport ω ⊆ V and covectorEuclideanNorm (ω(x) − G(x)) ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (G : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖) → IsOpen V → Continuous G → HasCompactSupport G → tsupport G ⊆ V → 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - G x) ≤ ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3, first bullet (approximating sequences): the rescaling argument around the sibling mollify_unit_field, stated for an arbitrary open set V and a single error ε > 0.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ (hypothesis). For a map F : ℝ^P → Λ and t ∈ ℝ, t•F is the pointwise multiple x ↦ t•F(x).
1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ Λ, |t•α| = ‖c(t•α)‖ = ‖t•c(α)‖ = |t|·‖c(α)‖ = |t|·|α|, because c is linear.
2. (Bound for G.) The map c∘G : ℝ^P → ℝ^d is continuous. Since c(0) = 0, support(c∘G) ⊆ support G, so c∘G has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). A continuous compactly supported map into a normed space is bounded (HasCompactSupport.exists_bound_of_continuous): there is C ∈ ℝ with ‖c(G(x))‖ ≤ C for all x. Put s := max(C, 0) + 1. Then s ≥ 1 > 0 and |G(x)| = ‖c(G(x))‖ ≤ C ≤ max(C, 0) ≤ s for every x.
3. (Normalized field.) Let g := s⁻¹•G, i.e. g(x) = s⁻¹•G(x). Then g is continuous. Since support g ⊆ support G, g has compact support and tsupport g ⊆ tsupport G ⊆ V. By steps 1–2, |g(x)| = s⁻¹·|G(x)| ≤ s⁻¹·s = 1 for every x.
4. (Mollification.) Apply the sibling mollify_unit_field (dor_ims_sua_mollify_unit_field) to V, g and the positive number ε/s; its hypotheses are verified in step 3. It gives an n-form ω₀ with IsTestForm ω₀, tsupport ω₀ ⊆ V, |ω₀(x)| ≤ 1 and |ω₀(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε/s for every x.
5. (Rescaling.) Put ω := s•ω₀. Test forms form a real vector subspace of the n-forms (testFormSubmodule), so IsTestForm ω. Since support ω ⊆ support ω₀, tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport ω₀ ⊆ V.
6. (Error.) For every x, ω(x) − G(x) = s•ω₀(x) − s•(s⁻¹•G(x)) = s•(ω₀(x) − g(x)), using s·s⁻¹ = 1 and linearity. By steps 1 and 4, |ω(x) − G(x)| = s·|ω₀(x) − g(x)| ≤ s·(ε/s) = ε.
7. By steps 5 and 6, ω satisfies IsTestForm ω, tsupport ω ⊆ V and covectorEuclideanNorm (ω(x) − G(x)) ≤ ε for all x ∈ ℝ^P.
proof_key_steps: |t•α| = |t|·|α| because |·| = ‖c ·‖; c∘G is continuous with compact support, hence |G| ≤ s := max(C, 0) + 1.
g := s⁻¹•G is continuous, compactly supported, tsupport g ⊆ V and |g| ≤ 1.
mollify_unit_field applied to g with error ε/s gives a test form ω₀ with tsupport ω₀ ⊆ V and |ω₀ − g| ≤ ε/s.
ω := s•ω₀ is a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ V and |ω − G| = s·|ω₀ − g| ≤ ε.

subproblems.title: Limit of T along test forms converging uniformly with supports in a fixed W ⊂⊂ U (parent steps 4–5)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ and let c : Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n → ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be a continuous linear equivalence with |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ for every α ∈ Λ. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and m : Set(ℝ^P) → ℝ a function such that |T(ω)| ≤ r·m(W) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained W U: closure W is compact and contained in U), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n), tsupport ω ⊆ W, r ∈ ℝ and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x. Then there is Φ : (ℝ^P → Λ) → ℝ such that T(ω_k) → Φ(G) as k → ∞ whenever G : ℝ^P → Λ, W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with W ⊂⊂ U, (ω_k) is a sequence in TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω_k ⊆ W for every k, and (ε_k) is a real sequence with ε_k → 0 and |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ ε_k for all k and x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (m : Set (Euclid P) → ℝ), (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖) → (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * m W) → ∃ Φ : (Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) → ℝ, ∀ (G : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn U n) (εs : ℕ → ℝ), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → (∀ k, tsupport (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W) → (∀ k x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x - G x) ≤ εs k) → Tendsto εs atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun k => T (ωs k)) atTop (𝓝 (Φ G))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 4 (Cauchy estimate) and 5 (definition of L(g) as a limit). In the parent, G = g̃, m(W) = (M_W(T)).toReal, and the parent discharges the hypothesis on m with its own prerequisite eval_mass_bound, which this child does not use. Here G is an arbitrary map and m an arbitrary function with the stated bound.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ (hypothesis); 'W ⊂⊂ U' means CompactlyContained W U, i.e. closure W is compact and closure W ⊆ U. For G : ℝ^P → Λ, a triple (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)) is approximating data for G if W is open, W ⊂⊂ U, every ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n has tsupport ω_k ⊆ W, |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ ε_k for all k and x, and ε_k → 0.
1. (Triangle inequality.) For α, β ∈ Λ, |α − β| = ‖c(α) − c(β)‖ ≤ ‖c(α)‖ + ‖c(β)‖ = |α| + |β|, because c is linear.
2. (Unions.) If W and W' are open with W ⊂⊂ U and W' ⊂⊂ U, then W ∪ W' is open. Also closure(W ∪ W') = closure W ∪ closure W' is compact (a union of two compact sets) and contained in U. So W ∪ W' ⊂⊂ U.
3. (Key estimate.) Let (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)) and (W', (ω'_l), (ε'_l)) be approximating data for the same G. Then for all k, l: |T(ω_k) − T(ω'_l)| ≤ (ε_k + ε'_l)·m(W ∪ W').
 Proof. Fix k, l and put δ := ω_k − ω'_l. TestFormOn U n is a real vector subspace, so δ ∈ TestFormOn U n, and its underlying form is x ↦ ω_k(x) − ω'_l(x). Since support δ ⊆ support ω_k ∪ support ω'_l, tsupport δ ⊆ tsupport ω_k ∪ tsupport ω'_l ⊆ W ∪ W'. For every x, δ(x) = (ω_k(x) − G(x)) − (ω'_l(x) − G(x)), so by step 1, |δ(x)| ≤ ε_k + ε'_l. By step 2, W ∪ W' is open and W ∪ W' ⊂⊂ U. The hypothesis on m, applied to W ∪ W', δ and r := ε_k + ε'_l, gives |T(δ)| ≤ (ε_k + ε'_l)·m(W ∪ W'). Finally, T(δ) = T(ω_k) − T(ω'_l) because T is linear.
4. (Convergence.) Let (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)) be approximating data for G and a_k := T(ω_k). Then (a_k) converges.
 Proof. Step 3, applied with both data equal to (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)), gives |a_k − a_l| ≤ (ε_k + ε_l)·m(W ∪ W) ≤ (|ε_k| + |ε_l|)·μ for all k, l, where μ := |m(W ∪ W)|. Let η > 0. Since ε_k → 0, there is N with |ε_k| < η/(2(μ + 1)) for all k ≥ N. Then for all k, l ≥ N, |a_k − a_l| ≤ (|ε_k| + |ε_l|)·μ ≤ μη/(μ + 1) < η, since μ ≥ 0 and μ/(μ + 1) < 1. So (a_k) is a Cauchy sequence of real numbers. Since ℝ is complete, (a_k) converges.
5. (Definition of Φ.) Let G : ℝ^P → Λ. If G admits approximating data, choose one such triple (W_G, (ω^G_k), (ε^G_k)) (axiom of choice) and set Φ(G) := lim_k T(ω^G_k). This limit exists by step 4. Otherwise set Φ(G) := 0.
6. (Every approximating sequence has limit Φ(G).) Let G, W, (ω_k) and (ε_k) satisfy the hypotheses of the conclusion. These say exactly that (W, (ω_k), (ε_k)) is approximating data for G. So the chosen triple (W_G, (ω^G_k), (ε^G_k)) exists, and T(ω^G_k) → Φ(G) by step 5. Step 3 with l = k gives 0 ≤ |T(ω_k) − T(ω^G_k)| ≤ (ε_k + ε^G_k)·m(W ∪ W_G), and the right-hand side tends to (0 + 0)·m(W ∪ W_G) = 0. Hence T(ω_k) − T(ω^G_k) → 0, and T(ω_k) = T(ω^G_k) + (T(ω_k) − T(ω^G_k)) → Φ(G) + 0 = Φ(G).
7. Hence Φ has the required property.
proof_key_steps: |·| = ‖c ·‖ satisfies the triangle inequality, and W ∪ W' ⊂⊂ U is open when W, W' are open and ⊂⊂ U.
For two approximating data of the same G, the hypothesis on m applied to ω_k − ω'_l on W ∪ W' gives |T(ω_k) − T(ω'_l)| ≤ (ε_k + ε'_l)·m(W ∪ W').
With equal data this makes (T(ω_k)) Cauchy, hence convergent in ℝ.
Define Φ(G) as the limit along chosen approximating data (0 if none exist).
The estimate with l = k shows that every approximating sequence of G has the same limit Φ(G).

subproblems.title: Linear extension of a locally bounded current to compactly supported continuous covector fields on ℝ^P (parent steps 2–3, 5–8)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n, d ∈ ℕ and let c : Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n → ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) be a continuous linear equivalence with |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ for every α ∈ Λ. Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), and m : Set(ℝ^P) → ℝ a function such that |T(ω)| ≤ r·m(W) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with W ⊂⊂ U (CompactlyContained W U), ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, tsupport ω ⊆ W, r ∈ ℝ and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x. Then there is Φ : (ℝ^P → Λ) → ℝ such that: (a) Φ(G₁ + G₂) = Φ(G₁) + Φ(G₂) whenever G₁, G₂ : ℝ^P → Λ are continuous with compact support and tsupport G_i ⊆ U; (b) Φ(t•G) = t·Φ(G) for every t ∈ ℝ and every continuous compactly supported G : ℝ^P → Λ with tsupport G ⊆ U; (c) Φ(ω) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n (ω regarded as the map ℝ^P → Λ); (d) |Φ(G)| ≤ r·m(W) whenever W ⊆ ℝ^P is open with W ⊂⊂ U, G : ℝ^P → Λ is continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ W, r ∈ ℝ, and |G(x)| ≤ r for all x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n d : ℕ) (c : Covector (Euclid P) n ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (m : Set (Euclid P) → ℝ), IsOpen U → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖) → (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * m W) → ∃ Φ : (Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) → ℝ, (∀ G₁ G₂ : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n, Continuous G₁ → HasCompactSupport G₁ → tsupport G₁ ⊆ U → Continuous G₂ → HasCompactSupport G₂ → tsupport G₂ ⊆ U → Φ (G₁ + G₂) = Φ G₁ + Φ G₂) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (G : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), Continuous G → HasCompactSupport G → tsupport G ⊆ U → Φ (t • G) = t * Φ G) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Φ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) = T ω) ∧ ∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (G : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (r : ℝ), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → Continuous G → HasCompactSupport G → tsupport G ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (G x) ≤ r) → |Φ G| ≤ r * m W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 2 (admissible open sets), 3 (approximating sequences), 5–6 (definition and linearity), 7 (agreement with T) and 8 (local bound), carried out on ℝ^P for compactly supported continuous covector fields G (in the parent, G = g̃). The bound M_W(T).toReal is replaced by m. The parent discharges the hypothesis on m with its own prerequisite eval_mass_bound, which this child does not use.
Notation: Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖c α‖ (hypothesis), so |α + β| ≤ |α| + |β| and |t•α| = |t|·|α| because c is linear; 'W ⊂⊂ U' means CompactlyContained W U. A map G : ℝ^P → Λ is admissible if it is continuous, has compact support and tsupport G ⊆ U. Sums and real multiples of maps ℝ^P → Λ are pointwise.
1. (Choice of Φ.) The hypotheses on c and m are exactly those of the sibling limit_functional (cmr_tfe_exists_limit_functional) for (P, n, d, c, U, T, m). It gives Φ : (ℝ^P → Λ) → ℝ with the following property (L). Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U, let ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω_k ⊆ W, and let |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ ε_k for all k and x, where ε_k → 0. Then T(ω_k) → Φ(G). Steps 4–7 prove (a)–(d) for this Φ.
2. (Topological facts.) (i) If S ⊆ U is compact, there is an open W with S ⊆ W, closure W ⊆ U and closure W compact, because ℝ^P is locally compact and regular and U is open (exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure). Thus W ⊂⊂ U. (ii) If W₁ and W₂ are open with W₁ ⊂⊂ U and W₂ ⊂⊂ U, then W₁ ∪ W₂ is open and W₁ ∪ W₂ ⊂⊂ U: closure(W₁ ∪ W₂) = closure W₁ ∪ closure W₂ is compact and contained in U. (iii) If W ⊂⊂ U, then W ⊆ closure W ⊆ U.
3. (Approximating sequences.) Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U, and let G be continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ W. For each k, the sibling uniform_approx (cmr_tfe_uniform_testForm_approx) with V := W and ε := 1/(k+1) > 0 gives a form ω_k with IsTestForm ω_k, tsupport ω_k ⊆ W and |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) for all x. By 2(iii), tsupport ω_k ⊆ U, so ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n. Since 1/(k+1) → 0, property (L) gives T(ω_k) → Φ(G). If G is admissible, then tsupport G is compact and contained in U, so 2(i) gives an open W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport G ⊆ W, and the above applies.
4. (Additivity (a).) Let G₁ and G₂ be admissible. By step 3, for i = 1, 2 choose an open W_i ⊂⊂ U and ω^i_k ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω^i_k ⊆ W_i, |ω^i_k(x) − G_i(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) and T(ω^i_k) → Φ(G_i). Put σ_k := ω¹_k + ω²_k ∈ TestFormOn U n. Then tsupport σ_k ⊆ tsupport ω¹_k ∪ tsupport ω²_k ⊆ W₁ ∪ W₂, and W₁ ∪ W₂ is open and ⊂⊂ U by 2(ii). For every x, σ_k(x) − (G₁ + G₂)(x) = (ω¹_k(x) − G₁(x)) + (ω²_k(x) − G₂(x)). Hence |σ_k(x) − (G₁ + G₂)(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) + 1/(k+1), which tends to 0. By (L), T(σ_k) → Φ(G₁ + G₂). Since T is linear, T(σ_k) = T(ω¹_k) + T(ω²_k) → Φ(G₁) + Φ(G₂). Limits in ℝ are unique, so Φ(G₁ + G₂) = Φ(G₁) + Φ(G₂).
5. (Homogeneity (b).) Let G be admissible and t ∈ ℝ. Take W and ω_k as in step 3, so T(ω_k) → Φ(G). Then t•ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport(t•ω_k) ⊆ tsupport ω_k ⊆ W. For every x, (t•ω_k)(x) − (t•G)(x) = t•(ω_k(x) − G(x)). So |(t•ω_k)(x) − (t•G)(x)| = |t|·|ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ |t|·(1/(k+1)), which tends to 0. By (L), T(t•ω_k) → Φ(t•G). By linearity, T(t•ω_k) = t·T(ω_k) → t·Φ(G). By uniqueness of limits, Φ(t•G) = t·Φ(G).
6. (Agreement (c).) Let ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Then IsTestForm ω, so ω has compact support and tsupport ω is compact; also tsupport ω ⊆ U. By 2(i), choose an open W ⊂⊂ U with tsupport ω ⊆ W. For G := ω, the constant sequence ω_k := ω with errors ε_k := 0 satisfies the hypotheses of (L), since |ω(x) − ω(x)| = |0| = 0 ≤ 0. So the constant sequence T(ω) tends to Φ(ω). It also tends to T(ω), so Φ(ω) = T(ω) by uniqueness of limits.
7. (Bound (d).) Let W be open with W ⊂⊂ U, let G be continuous with compact support and tsupport G ⊆ W, let r ∈ ℝ, and let |G(x)| ≤ r for all x. Step 3, applied to W and G, gives ω_k ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω_k ⊆ W, |ω_k(x) − G(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) and T(ω_k) → Φ(G). For every x, ω_k(x) = (ω_k(x) − G(x)) + G(x), so |ω_k(x)| ≤ 1/(k+1) + r. The hypothesis on m, applied to W, ω_k and r + 1/(k+1), gives |T(ω_k)| ≤ (r + 1/(k+1))·m(W) for every k. As k → ∞, |T(ω_k)| → |Φ(G)| (continuity of the absolute value) and (r + 1/(k+1))·m(W) → r·m(W). Non-strict inequalities are preserved under limits, so |Φ(G)| ≤ r·m(W).
8. Steps 4–7 prove (a)–(d) for Φ.
proof_key_steps: Take Φ from limit_functional: T(ω_k) → Φ(G) along every sequence approximating G uniformly with supports in a fixed open W ⊂⊂ U.
Every compact S ⊆ U lies in an open W ⊂⊂ U, and unions of two such sets stay ⊂⊂ U.
uniform_approx with errors 1/(k+1) gives an approximating sequence for every continuous compactly supported G with tsupport G ⊆ W.
Sums and real multiples of approximating sequences approximate G₁ + G₂ (on W₁ ∪ W₂) and t•G, so (a) and (b) hold by linearity of T and uniqueness of limits.
The constant sequence ω gives Φ(ω) = T(ω).
|ω_k| ≤ r + 1/(k+1) and the m-bound give |T(ω_k)| ≤ (r + 1/(k+1))·m(W), hence |Φ(G)| ≤ r·m(W) in the limit.
